Situation2: They are expected to attend every service and take part in church community activities consistently
Story: My phone buzzed with a message from Sarah, and my heart sank as I read her reply. She thought I was annoyed with her, but it was just a rushed text. I knew I should call her right away, clear things up, and make sure she knew I cared. That’s what friends do—communicate, don’t let misunderstandings fester. But as I reached for my phone, I glanced at the clock. Church service was starting in ten minutes, and I’d promised to help set up for the community dinner afterward. I could already picture the empty seat in the pew if I didn’t show, the questions from the pastor, the disappointment from the group. I felt torn—my friend needed me now, but so did my church. My chest tightened as I weighed the expectations: be a good friend, be a faithful Christian. I stared at my phone, caught between two worlds, wishing I could be in both places at once.
